# Set up Tether

You are an AI agent helping a person install Tether on the computer you run on.
Tether is a self-hosted chat UI for coding agents in tmux: Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity. The server runs on the person's machine. There is no Tether account or cloud.
Source: https://github.com/incmak/tether (MIT). Human guide: https://incmak.github.io/tether/

## Rules

1. Show the installer plan and wait for an explicit yes before you run `--apply`. Only Step 2 writes before the yes, and only the files it lists.
2. Never print, copy, or send the access token. Give only the path of the token file.
3. Do not expose the server to the internet. Do not bind it to 0.0.0.0 unless the person chooses a trusted LAN after you state the warning below.
4. Stop if a download or checksum fails. Do not fall back to an unverified archive or a git clone of main.
5. Do not write service files or agent settings yourself. `install.py` does that.
6. If you cannot run commands, give the person one step at a time and ask them to paste the output with any secrets removed.

## Shortcut for Claude Code

If you are Claude Code and the plugin is available, tell the person they can run these instead, then stop:

    /plugin marketplace add incmak/tether
    /plugin install tether@tether

Then they type `set up tether`.

## Step 1: Check requirements

- Linux with a systemd user session, or macOS. Android (Termux) has a separate path: see "Android" below.
- Python 3.11 or newer. The macOS system Python is too old; use Homebrew Python.
- tmux, and at least one of `claude`, `codex`, `agy`.
- No root needed. No Node needed for a release install.

Report what is missing and how to install it. Ask before you install anything.

## Step 2: Download a verified release

    curl -fL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/incmak/tether/v0.1.11/integrations/claude/tether/skills/setup/bootstrap.py -o tether-bootstrap.py
    python3 tether-bootstrap.py

Tell the person what this writes before you run it: the script in the current folder, and the release files under `~/.local/share/tether`.
This downloads the latest stable release and SHA256SUMS, checks SHA-256, and links `~/.local/share/tether/current`. It starts no services, installs no dependencies, and changes no settings.
If `~/.config/tether/install.json` shows an existing git checkout install, stop and ask. Use `python3 ~/.local/share/tether/current/tether migrate` only after a yes.

## Step 3: Show the baseline plan

    python3 ~/.local/share/tether/current/install.py --plan --json --no-build-ui

A plan writes nothing. Show the URL, host, auth, ports, features, updates, checks, warnings, and `cli_link`. A zero exit code alone does not prove readiness: read every check, and show failed checks with their `fix` text.

Tell the person the defaults. On a first install, the plan turns on the interactive terminal if `ttyd` is on PATH. All other features are off. On a later install, saved choices apply. Step 4 can change any of these.

In `hooks`, read `path` and `action`. An action that starts with `preserve` leaves that file unchanged. Any other action changes it. Ignore the separate `remove` and `replace` fields: they are internal to `--apply`.

## Step 4: Ask once for choices

Features (any): interactive terminal (`--terminal`, needs ttyd), voice-to-text (`--voice`), push notifications (`--push`, needs HTTPS), usage hooks (`--hooks`), host resources (`--resources`), small photos (`--images`, installs Pillow). Pass `--no-<feature>` for each one not chosen.

Remote access (one):

| Choice | Flags | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tailscale (recommended for a phone) | `--host 127.0.0.1 --auth token` | Encrypted. HTTPS through Tailscale Serve. |
| HTTPS reverse proxy | `--host 127.0.0.1 --auth proxy` | The proxy must require sign-in. |
| Same trusted Wi-Fi | `--host 0.0.0.0 --auth token` | Warning: plain HTTP sends the token and chat without encryption. Push and home-screen install do not work. |
| This computer only | `--host 127.0.0.1 --auth token` | A phone cannot reach it. |

Updates (one): `--updates notify` (recommended), `--updates auto`, or `--updates off`.
If the plan lists `legacy_units`, ask keep or replace. Add `--replace-legacy` only for replace.

## Step 5: Review, then apply

1. Run the plan again with the chosen flags and `--no-build-ui`. Keep the baseline port through `--port`.
2. Show what changes. State that apply can install dependencies, save choices, and start or restart services.
3. Resolve failed checks. Then ask for an explicit yes.
4. After the yes, run the same command with `--apply` in place of `--plan`.
5. Report a failed command as a failure.

## Step 6: Finish

Give the person the `url` and `token_file` from the result. They sign in at `/chat/` with the token in that file.

- Tailscale: both devices must be in the same tailnet, with MagicDNS and HTTPS Certificates on (admin console, DNS page). The person runs `tailscale serve --bg --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, then opens the printed HTTPS address with `/chat/` added.
- Reverse proxy: see https://github.com/incmak/tether/blob/main/server/deploy/examples/nginx-auth-proxy.conf
- Same Wi-Fi: open `http://<computer-LAN-IP>:<port>/chat/`.

Then tell the person to run `tmux new -s work`, start `claude`, `codex`, or `agy` inside it, and select the session in Tether.
If `~/.local/bin` is not on PATH, give them: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`.
On Linux, for services that must survive logout, give them: `loginctl enable-linger $USER`. It can need admin permission; do not run it yourself.
Installer success does not prove phone access. Ask the person to test it from the phone.

## After setup

- Install as an app, on an HTTPS address only. Android Chrome: More, Install and create shortcut, Install. iPhone Safari: Share, Add to Home Screen. Desktop Chrome: More, Cast, save, and share, Install page as app.
- Add another machine: install Tether there too. In Tether, select the host name at the bottom of the sidebar, select "Add a host", and type its address. Each host opens at its own address with its own sign-in.
- Update: **Update now** in the sidebar, or `tether update --yes`. Go back with `tether rollback`.
- Remove: run `install.py --plan --uninstall`, then `--apply --uninstall`. This keeps tokens and data.

## Android

Termux from F-Droid or GitHub, not Google Play:

    pkg install python tmux nodejs git ttyd termux-services
    git clone https://github.com/incmak/tether.git
    cd tether
    python install.py --plan --no-voice
    python install.py --apply --no-voice
    termux-wake-lock

Voice and automatic updates do not work on Termux. Agent CLIs on Termux are not tested.
